rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sabbath was specially assigned to them; a report says they were offered Friday, chose Saturday, received it as a feast with work forbidden, then disobeyed and were destroyed.
rows.anchor: الجمعة، فقالوا: نريد يوم السبت، فجعل لهم يوم السبت عيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sabbath restriction was a trial whose benefit followed their sin, like many Islamic laws; it was not punishment, since a duty can yield great reward.
rows.anchor: كان ابتلاء إلا أن مصلحتهم في ذلك أن يكون ابتلاء عقيب الفسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgression was their own deed, refuting the Mujbira doctrine that human acts are created by God.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الاعتداء كان فعلهم، فيبطل قول المجبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentator counts eleven readings for بئيس: five among the seven canonical readings and six outside them.
rows.anchor: بئيس إحدى عشرة قراءة، خمس في السبع، وست خارج السبع

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع
rows.claim: Abu Jaafar and Nafi read بيس with kasra on the yāʾ and no hamza, on the pattern فعل.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة أبي جعفر ونافع

rows.speaker: خارجة عن نافع
rows.claim: Another reading has kasra on bāʾ, a quiescent yāʾ, and no hamza, like ليل.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة خارجة عن نافع

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads بئس with kasra on bāʾ and hamza, like بئر.
rows.anchor: نحو: بئر، وهي قراءة ابن عامر

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abu Bakr from Asim reads بيأس with fatḥa on bāʾ and hamza, on the pattern فيعل.
rows.anchor: على وزن (فيعل) نحو: صيقل، أبو بكر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers use بئيس on فعيل; this is the common and best-known form, and its adjectival pattern is preferred by Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim.
rows.anchor: ابن كثير، وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim prefer فعيل because it better fits adjectives and is the most familiar form.
rows.anchor: وهو اختيار أبي عبيد وأبي حاتم؛ لأن فعيل أشبه بالصفات والنعوت

rows.speaker: ذو الأصبع العدواني
rows.claim: Dhu al-Isba al-Adwani's line uses بئيس as evidence for the adjective reading.
rows.anchor: قال ذو الأصبع العدواني: حنقا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads بيس with kasra on bāʾ and fatḥa on the final sīn, meaning the punishment is bad.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن (بيس) بكسر الباء وفتح السين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads بايس on the pattern فاعل.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد (بايس) على وزن (فاعل)

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads بيس with fatḥa on bāʾ and yāʾ, without hamza, on فعل like جمل.
rows.anchor: عن أبي (بيس) بفتح الباء والياء

rows.speaker: نصر بن عاصم
rows.claim: Nasr ibn Asim reads بيس with fatḥa on bāʾ, a doubled kasra-yāʾ, and no hamza, on فعل like جيد.
rows.anchor: عن نصر بن عاصم بفتح الباء وكسر الياء مشددا

rows.speaker: بعض أهل مكة
rows.claim: Some Meccans read بيس with kasra on bāʾ and no hamza, like ليل, on فعل.
rows.anchor: عن بعض أهل مكة (بيس) بكسر الباء غير الهمزة

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم وعمر بن الخطاب وأبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu Bakr from Asim, Umar, and Abu al-Aliya read يمسكون with a light mīm, from يمسك.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم يمسكون مخففة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the doubled form, preferred by Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim: مسكت بالشيء but أمسكته without bi.
rows.anchor: قرأ الباقون بالتشديد، وهو اختيار أبي عبيد، وأبي حاتم

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Amash has the variant والذين استمسكوا بالكتاب.
rows.anchor: وعن الأعمش: والذين استمسكوا بالكتاب

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kab reads تمسكوا بالقراءة.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب: تمسكوا بالقراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading درسوا means that they read the Scripture.
rows.anchor: والقراءة الظاهرة: ودرسوا ما فيه يعني قرؤوا

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulami reads ادارسوا, meaning they studied together and read to one another, as in ادّاركوا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي: ادارسوا أي: تدارسوا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The public reading has يعقلون in third person; al-Hasan reads تعقلون as direct address.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن بالتاء على الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the apparent, widely transmitted reading is admissible; anomalous forms may reflect a reading error, poor recitation, or belief that Quran may be read in all languages.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز القراءة إلا بالظاهر والمستفيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Quran means only the widely transmitted text, the objection about anomalous readings disappears.
rows.anchor: القرآن هو المنقول المستفيض دون ما سواه، فلا شبهة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a quiescent lām, خلف means a successor; with fatḥa, خلف is a replacement received for what was taken away.
rows.anchor: الخلف بسكون اللام: من يجيء بعد، والخلف بفتحها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra cites the expressions خلف سوء and خلف صدق as usage examples.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: يقال: خلف سوء، وخلف صدق

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi reverses the usual distinction: fatḥa means righteous successor and sukūn means wicked successor.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: الخلف بالفتح: الصالح، وبالسكون: الطالح

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid compares a خلف to the skin of a scabbed person as evidence for the term's usage.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد: وبقيت في خلف كجلد الأجرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sukūn form is more often blameworthy, perhaps deriving from milk left until spoiled; the fatḥa form is usually praise, though the forms can substitute for each other.
rows.anchor: الأغلب على الخلف بالسكون أن يستعمل في الذم

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Ali ibn Isa says the two forms may be used in place of each other.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن عيسى: وقد يوضع أحدهما مكان الآخر

rows.speaker: حسان
rows.claim: Hassan's line uses خلفنا positively for a successor who follows the first generation in obeying God.
rows.anchor: [قال حسان]: لنا القدم الأولى إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An عرض is something that appears and does not remain long; the philosophical term for accident reflects that it appears in bodies without permanence, and clouds are also called عرض.
rows.anchor: والعرض: ما يعرض، ويقل لبثه

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and al-Kisai read طيف without an alif; the Nakhai and al-Aswad ibn Yazid also read it so.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي: طيف بغير ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use طائف with an alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون طائف بالألف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj cites طفت عليه and طاف الخيال; الطائف is like a passing thought or occurrence.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: طفت عليه أطوف، وطاف الخيال يطيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats الطيف and الطائف as synonyms, like الميت and المائت; another distinguishes them.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا فقيل: الطيف والطائف واحد، كالميت والمائت

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع
rows.claim: Abu Jaafar and Nafi read يمدونهم with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on mīm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع: يمدونهم بضم الياء وكسر الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on mīm; both are Arabic forms, مد يمد and أمد يمد.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: يمدونهم بفتح الياء وضم الميم، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view makes مد mean pulling them into misguidance; أمد means adding further evil to an already evil state, leaving no hope of success.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مد: جذب، يعني بخروجهم إلى الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicon also uses مددته for extending something and مديد for a tall man.
rows.anchor: ويقال: مددت الشيء مدا، ورجل مديد: طويل القامة

rows.speaker: الجحدري
rows.claim: Al-Jahdari has the variant يمادونهم.
rows.anchor: وعن الجحدري: يمادونهم

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: The common reading is يقصرون with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on ṣād; Isa ibn Umar uses fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on ṣād, both dialect forms.
rows.anchor: وعن عيسى بن عمر يقصرون بفتح الياء وضم الصاد، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مس means touching by hand; related uses describe one afflicted by touch and water reached by hands.
rows.anchor: المس: مس الشيء بيدك، يقال: مسسته أمسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طيف derives from the wāw-root طاف; a doubled form may also have been lightened, like كيد and ميت.
rows.anchor: الطيف أصله الواو، ويقال: طاف يطوف طوفا وطوافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses يطيف as evidence for the word's form.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: أنى ألم بك الخيال يطيف

rows.speaker: ابن فارس وابن عرفة
rows.claim: Ibn Faris and Ibn Arafa define الطيف and الطائف alike as a jinn or apparition hovering around a person.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس وابن عرفة: الطيف والطائف

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وأبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Amr and Abu Ubayd distinguish them: الطائف is Satan's whispering, while الطيف is madness.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو وأبو عبيد: الطائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayy is misguidance that brings disappointment, opposite right guidance; its root sense is failure.
rows.anchor: والغي: الضلال الذي يورث الخيبة، والغي: نقيض الرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line says whoever fails will not lack a blamer for his failure.
rows.anchor: ومن يغو لا يعدم على الغي لائما أي: من يخب

rows.speaker: ابن عرفة
rows.claim: قصر means refraining; أقصر is stopping despite ability, قصر عنه can mean weakness or inability, and قصر من الشيء can mean diminishing it, as in shortening prayer.
rows.anchor: القصر: الكف عن الشيء، يقال: قصر من الشيء: إذا كف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses لأقصر القلب to mean that his heart would desist if not held by attachments.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: لولا علائق من نعم علقت بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quran derives from gathering: stars gather, menstrual blood gathers in the womb, and blood gathers in the body during purity; recitation is reading and its root sense is following.
rows.anchor: القرآن: أصله الجمع، ومنه قرأت النجوم: اجتمعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inṣāt means refraining from speech.
rows.anchor: والإنصات: الإمساك عن الكلام، أنصت ينصت إنصاتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: القرآن is nominative as the subject substitute of a passive verb, since the verb is predicated of it.
rows.anchor: رفع القرآن لأنه اسم ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لعل expresses hope or expectation and can also mean the purpose particle كي.
rows.anchor: و(لعل) كلمة رجاء وطمع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وأبو هريرة والزهري ومجاهد والضحاك والسدي والحسن وقتادة وعبيد بن عمير وعطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: These authorities say the verse was revealed about prayer, where people spoke and greeted one another and were then ordered to listen.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت الآية في الصلاة، وكانوا يتكلمون فيها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that it was revealed about an Anṣārī youth who recited along whenever the Prophet recited.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة أنه أنزلت في فتى من الأنصار

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وجماعة
rows.claim: Another report places the revelation in the context of the Friday sermon.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت الآية في الخطبة، عن سعيد بن جبير وجماعة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة والكلبي
rows.claim: Another report connects it to raised voices behind the Prophet during prayer when Paradise and Hell were mentioned.
rows.anchor: ذكر الجنة والنار، عن أبي هريرة والكلبي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says it answered polytheists who told one another to ignore the Quran and make noise when it was recited.
rows.anchor: نزلت الآية جوابا لهم، عن سعيد بن المسيب

rows.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: When asked, Ahmad ibn Hanbal said the community agreed that the verse was revealed about prayer.
rows.anchor: وسئل أحمد بن حنبل عن ذلك، فقال

rows.speaker: شيخنا أبو حامد
rows.claim: Abu Hamid links the command to the preceding description of Quran as insight, guidance, and mercy: listening and reflection lead to truth.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم أن القرآن بصائر وهدى ورحمة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says this completes the Prophet's answer to polytheists asking about the Hour and signs: the Quran is inimitable, so they should listen and reflect.
rows.anchor: إن القرآن معجز، فإذا قرئ فاستمعوا فتدبروا لتعلموا، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن والزهري
rows.claim: The common reading has a light hamzated rāʾ and fatḥa on mīm; al-Hasan doubles rāʾ without hamza, while al-Zuhri has ḍamma on mīm with hamza; all are dialect forms.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: بين المرء وقلبه بفتح الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: استجابة and إجابة are synonymous; another view makes istijāba seeking an answer, though the cited line uses it to mean answering.
rows.anchor: الاستجابة والإجابة بمعنى، وقيل: الاستجابة: طلب الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses فلم يستجبه to mean that no one answered the caller.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna originally means trial or examination, then is used for punishment, civil disorder, and disbelief.
rows.anchor: والفتنة: أصلها الاختبار والامتحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāṣṣa is what belongs to you without others; its opposite is generality.
rows.anchor: والخاصة: ما كان لك من شيء دون غيرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis treats لا تصيبن as a prohibition after a command, not its response, since a response would not take the emphatic nūn; it implies إذا.
rows.anchor: أن قوله: لا تصيبن ليس بجواب، ولكنه نهي بعد أمر

rows.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
rows.claim: Some Kufans analyze لا تصيبن on the pattern of an oath response, with a conditional aspect despite being a prohibition.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكوفيين: أمرهم ثم نهاهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the warning was revealed specifically about the Prophet's Companions.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في أصحاب النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - خاصة، عن ابن عباس

words: فتنة لا تصيبن الذين ظلموا منكم خاصة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers were told not to tolerate wrongdoing among them, lest punishment encompass them all.
rows.anchor: أمر الله المؤمنين ألا يقروا المنكر بين أظهرهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan identifies Ali, Ammar, Talha, and al-Zubayr as addressed; al-Zubayr says they later realized they were meant after opposing one another and being struck by the fitna.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: نزلت في علي وعمار وطلحة والزبير

rows.speaker: السدي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and Muqatil say the verse concerned only the people of Badr, and that the fitna struck them at the Battle of the Camel.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي ومقاتل: نزلت في أهل بدر خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view places the verse at Uthman's killing and limits the fitna to his killers and those who fought Ali.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في قتل عثمان، وإنما تكون الفتنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands compliance with His call and warns against disobeying His command.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر - تعالى - بإجابة دعائه وحذر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Zajjaj gloss استجيبوا as أجيبوا; answering God means obeying His commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: قيل: أجيبوا، عن أبي عبيدة والزجاج. وإجابته طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is to persist in obedience whenever God and the Messenger call; the lām means إلى.
rows.anchor: داوموا على ما أنتم عليه من الإجابة لله وللرسول

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says faith gives life after their death in disbelief, so the call is to faith and obedience, the life of the soul.
rows.anchor: الإيمان يحييهم بعد موتهم أي كفرهم، عن السدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains what gives life as the truth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلى الحق، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also identifies it as Quran, which brings life, salvation, and protection in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: هو القرآن في الحياة والنجاة والعصمة في الدنيا والآخرة، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق والفراء وأبو علي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq, al-Farra, and Abu Ali say it is jihad, which revives their cause and exalts their religion through God's support against the enemy.
rows.anchor: هو الجهاد؛ أي: دعاكم إلى إحياء أمركم وإعزاز دينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is knowledge and action, through which people find guidance and attain ranks.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو العلم والعمل، أي: يحييكم بالعلم والعمل

rows.speaker: القتبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutbi says it means martyrdom and cites the promise that martyrs are alive with their Lord and provided for.
rows.anchor: الشهادة، عن [القتبي]، وقرأ: (بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون)

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says it is the Garden and the lasting life and eternal bliss it entails.
rows.anchor: إلى الجنة وما يورثكم فيها من الحياة الدائمة ونعيم الأبد، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: أبو علي وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Ali and Abu Muslim say God prevents benefit from the heart through death, loss of reason, or another affliction, so missed opportunities cannot be recovered; this urges prompt obedience.
rows.anchor: يفرق بين المرء والانتفاع بقلبه بالموت أو إذهاب اللب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that God stands between a person and what the heart wishes: lifespan blocks hope and decree blocks planning.
rows.anchor: يحول بين المرء وبين ما يتمناه ويريد بقلبه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes it to mean God is nearer than the jugular vein and nothing is hidden from Him; this is a grave warning.
rows.anchor: أراد أنه أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد لا يخفى عليه

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm says God turns hearts between states: the Companions feared death in jihad, so God would replace fear with security by intervening between them and that fear.
rows.anchor: وأعلمهم الله أنه يبدل خوفهم أمنا بأن يحول بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It cannot mean that God prevents belief: He calls people to faith, promises reward and threatens for rejecting it, so the servant must be the responder rather than God answering His own call.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز حمله على المنع من الإيمان؛ لأن الظاهر بخلافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All are gathered for recompense, good for good and evil for evil; therefore one must hasten to obedience and repentance.
rows.anchor: تجمعون إلى الجزاء إن خيرا فخير، وإن شرا فشر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers use kasra on ʿayn in both instances of العدوة; the other readers use ḍamma, and both are dialects.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: (بالعدوة) بكسر العين في الحرفين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم والبزي عن ابن كثير وبصير عن الكسائي ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the two yāʾs distinctly in ويحيا.
rows.anchor: ويعقوب ويحيا من حيي بإظهار الياءين

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير وابن فليح وابن عامر وحمزة وحفص عن عاصم والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers assimilate the two yāʾs into a doubled yāʾ; the second has a fixed vowel and the written form has one yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير في رواية القراءتين، وابن فليح وابن عامر وحمزة وحفص عن عاصم والكسائي بياء مشددة على الإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Distinct pronunciation follows the related imperfect يحيى; Basrans reject assimilation in حيا يحيا since even a sound doubled verb favors clarity when its second radical is quiescent, and some Kufans allow assimilation.
rows.anchor: فأما الإظهار فلامتناع الإدغام في مضارعه من يحيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿidwa is a side of a valley; its two sides are its edges and boundaries.
rows.anchor: العدوة: جانب الوادي، والجميع عداء وللوادي عدوتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-quṣwā is the feminine of al-aqṣā, like al-kubrā and al-ṣughrā.
rows.anchor: والقصوى تأنيث الأقصى كالأكبر والكبرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here الدنيا means nearer toward Mecca; the word also means the first life and derives from wāw, changed to yāʾ for ease.
rows.anchor: والدنيا تأنيث الأدنى، يعني أدنى إلى جهة مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قصي denotes distance: القصوى is farthest, أقصيته means moved away, and قصوت من القوم means kept apart.
rows.anchor: والقصي: البعد، وهو بالمكان الأقصى: الأبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukb is a collective plural of rider, equivalent to rukbān; it describes people on camels, and related forms denote a rideable she-camel or a colt fit to ride.
rows.anchor: والركب: جمع راكب، كشارب وشرب، ركب يركب ركوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sufl means lower, the opposite of high, with related forms سفل and تسفل.
rows.anchor: والسفل: خلاف العلو، سفل يسفل سفالا وتسفل تسفلا

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub reads وما يؤخره with yāʾ, referring to God in وكذلك أخذ ربك; others use first-person plural nun in narration.
rows.anchor: قرأ يعقوب: وما يؤخره بالياء

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Asim, and Hamza delete the yāʾ in يأت; other readers retain the original form.
rows.anchor: يوم يأت بحذف الياء ابن عامر، وعاصم، وحمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deleting the yāʾ lightens the form and relies on kasra; Arabs let kasra stand for yāʾ and ḍamma for wāw, following the written text; Ibn Kathir retains it in both positions.
rows.anchor: والحذف على التخفيف، والاجتزاء بالكسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading of إذا أخذ has an alif after ذال; some read it without alif as a past tense.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: إذا أخذ بألف بعد الذال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaṣīd means harvested, a passive فعيل: crops cut from the root; it can also mean killing people with a sword.
rows.anchor: الحصيد: المحصود، فعيل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabāb is loss and tatbīb is causing loss; تبا means destruction, as in the curse on Abu Lahab.
rows.anchor: والتباب: الخسران، والتتبيب: التخسير

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir's line uses تبا and تبابا for ruin and destruction.
rows.anchor: قال جرير: عرادة من بقية قوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ajal is the appointed time for an event to occur.
rows.anchor: والأجل: الوقت المضروب لوقوع أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shiqāʾ is strength of the causes of affliction; related forms mean enduring hardship because one suffers through it.
rows.anchor: والشقاء: قوة أسباب البلاء، رجل شقي بين الشقوة والشقوة والشقاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿāda is strength of the causes of blessing; saʿd means good fortune.
rows.anchor: والسعادة: قوة أسباب النعمة، والسعد: اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك points either to the report about the towns or to the revelation itself.
rows.anchor: (ذلك) إشارة إلى النبأ، تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows from the womb who will disobey and be wretched and who will obey and be happy; this does not mean He makes an innocent person wretched without sin, which would invite blame without cause.
rows.anchor: فالله يعلم أنه شقي، وهو في بطن أمه يعلم أنه يعصي

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar's report says each person is facilitated for what he was created to do; the author takes this as creation for obedience and enablement for it.
rows.anchor: وما روي في خبر عمر: كل ميسر لما خلق له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the purpose of creation as worship as evidence that people were created for obedience.
rows.anchor: وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون (56)

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet's report says every newborn is born upon the natural disposition.
rows.anchor: وقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: كل مولود يولد على الفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zafīr is repeated breathing with sound and grief until the ribs swell; its root connotes intensity, with related uses for heavy loads, binding, a roaring fire, and water carriers.
rows.anchor: الزفير: ترديد النفس مع الصوت مع الحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account reverses the breath terms: shahiq is drawing breath back in and zafīr is breathing it out.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الزفير الشهيق؛ لأن الشهيق رد النفس

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Ali ibn Isa describes shahiq as a dreadful deep sound during extended breathing; its root suggests excessive length, as in جبل شاهق.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن عيسى، وأصله: الطول المفرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another distinction makes zafīr the first donkey bray and shahiq its last.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الزفير: أول نهاق الحمير، والشهيق: آخر نهاقها

rows.speaker: ابن عرفة
rows.claim: Ibn Arafa says zafīr comes from the chest and shahiq from the throat; both are sounds of sufferers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عرفة: والزفير من الصدر، والشهيق من الحلق

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Hafs from Asim read سُعدوا with ḍamma; the others use fatḥa in parallel with شقوا.
rows.anchor: حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص عن عاصم: سعدوا بضم السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍamma is explained as deletion of the augment in أسعدوا, since the verb is intransitive; سعد and أسعد are synonymous, like forms where an augment is removed.
rows.anchor: وإنما جاز ضم السين؛ لأنه على حذف الزيادة من أسعدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jadh means cutting; majdhood means cut, and a hadith describes eating a jad hīdha, a sip of sawīq named for being crumbled.
rows.anchor: والجذ: القطع، والمجذوذ: المقطوع، وجذه: قطعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says he ate a small portion of sawīq before setting out; it was called jad hīdha because it is crumbled.
rows.anchor: أنه كان يأكل جذيذة قبل أن يغدو في حاجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in ما دامت is a verbal noun, meaning a duration like the duration of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: المصدر بتقدير: يدوم كدوام السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عطاء is accusative as a verbal noun meaning He gave a gift and also functions circumstantially; خالدين is likewise circumstantial and accusative.
rows.anchor: نصب على المصدر، أي: أعطاهم عطاء، فهو حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After saying that people are wretched or happy, the passage describes each group's state; the wretched enter Hell deserving punishment as recompense for their deeds.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر القيامة، وأن منهم شقي وسعيد، بين حال كل واحد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says zafīr is the loud sound and shahiq the weak sound.
rows.anchor: الصوت الشديد، والشهيق: الصوت الضعيف، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مقاتل والضحاك
rows.claim: Muqatil and al-Dahhak say zafīr is the beginning of a donkey's bray and shahiq its last sound as it ends and echoes in its throat.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل والضحاك. قال قتادة: صوت الكافر في النار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada compares the disbeliever's voice in Hell to a donkey's: it begins with zafīr and ends with shahiq.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: صوت الكافر في النار صوت الحمار

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya locates zafīr in the throat and shahiq in the chest.
rows.anchor: الزفير في الحلق، والشهيق في الصدر، عن أبي العالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations take the sounds as cries of woe or continual weeping from the severity of their plight, the latter reported by the Qadi.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو أصواته بالويل والثبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned remain in Hell; God does whatever He wills and no obstacle can prevent Him.
rows.anchor: يفعل ما يريد لا يمنعه مانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss says no new considerations appear to God because He already knows all things.
rows.anchor: لا تبدو له البدوات؛ لأنه عالم بالأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The happy remain in Paradise permanently, except as God wills; their gift is uncut, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak explain.
rows.anchor: وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak gloss غير مجذوذ as not cut off.
rows.anchor: غير مجذوذ أي: غير مقطوع، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In response to the objection that reward and punishment are eternal, he gives two views: these very heavens and earth, or an expression of indefinitely long duration.
rows.anchor: اختلف العلماء فيه على قولين: الأول: المراد بالسماوات والأرض هن هذه السماوات والأرض بعينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats the exception as possible expulsion without intent: God could expel them but ruled they remain; al-Hasan says the exception emphasizes that God willed their permanence.
rows.anchor: وسادسها: أنه استثناء من الإخراج، وهو لا يريد إخراجهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the exception concerns added bliss for Paradise's people and added torment for Hell's people.
rows.anchor: وسابعها: أن الاستثناء وقع على الزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes إلا as و, a common usage; the cited verse then means neither wrongdoers are exempt, and both groups remain forever.
rows.anchor: بمعنى الواو، وذلك شائع في اللغة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: For those who distinguish the groups, one reading has God release monotheists from Hell; Abu Majliz says He may forgive them before entry and may delay the happy before admitting them to Paradise.
rows.anchor: أن يخرج أهل التوحيد منها. روي ذلك عن ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God specified what He wills for Paradise's people as an uncut gift, but did not specify His will for Hell's people.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أخبرنا بالذي يشاء لأهل الجنة فقال

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the exception is time in Hell before entry to Paradise; the author rejects this because the clauses for both groups have the same structure, so permanence for one entails it for the other.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك: إلا ما مكثوا في النار حتى أدخلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes the exception disconnected, meaning but for an increase, as in the phrase except Iblis.
rows.anchor: هذا الاستثناء منقطع، وأكثر ما يكون ذلك كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing wretchedness and happiness to people shows they act for themselves, refuting the claim that a person is wretched before birth.
rows.anchor: يدل قوله: شقوا وسعدوا أن الشقاوة والسعادة فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every wretched person is in Hell, including a sinner, contrary to the Murji'a.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن كل شقي في النار وإن كان فاسقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The uncut gift proves Paradise lasts forever, contrary to Jahm; both verses support eternal residence, with stronger emphasis in this phrase.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله:عطاء غير مجذوذ على دوام الجنة
